chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, who said: 'I heard Bukeyr ibn Ayn narrating from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).'

He said: 'The one who commits adultery with a close female relative (mahram) until he consummates it with her, is struck with one strike of the sword, which takes from him what it takes (life or death). And if she was the one pursuing him, she is struck with one strike of the sword, which takes from her what it takes.' It was said to him: 'So who strikes them both, when there is no adversary for the two of them?' He said: 'That is upon the Imam, when the matter is raised to him.'

key_terms.ذَاتِ مَحْرَمٍ: Close female relative (mahram) with whom marriage is permanently forbidden
key_terms.ضَرْبَةً بِالسَّيْفِ: A single strike of the sword

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for incest with a close relative according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the specific penalty of death by the sword (qatl bi-l-sayf) for incest with a mahram, distinguishing it from general zina by emphasizing the Imam's authority to execute the ruling even without a plaintiff (ghayr al-mukhtas). The phrase 'took what it took' indicates a single, decisive strike that severs the head, reflecting the severity of violating close kinship ties. This ruling underscores the Imam's role in maintaining social order by acting as the public prosecutor in cases where the parties themselves do not sue.
